description: Double-ended queue (deque) bookkeeping atoms modelled as a direct extension of the safe_queue.mm pattern. Proves the len <= cap invariant for push/pop on both ends using Z3 integer theory — no array theory required. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/container/deque — verified double-ended queue'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/container/safe_queue.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/container/safe_queue.mm already use (checked_add, checked_sub, conditional expressions).

atoms.name: deque_push_front
atoms.description: Push an element onto the front of the deque. Requires len < cap so the invariant len <= cap is preserved. Mirrors enqueue but from the opposite end.

atoms.name: deque_push_back
atoms.description: Push an element onto the back of the deque. Identical bookkeeping to enqueue.

atoms.name: deque_pop_front
atoms.description: Pop the front element of a non-empty deque.

atoms.name: deque_pop_back
atoms.description: Pop the back element of a non-empty deque.

atoms.name: deque_is_empty
atoms.description: Return 1 when the deque has no elements, 0 otherwise.

atoms.name: deque_remaining
atoms.description: Spare capacity of the deque (cap - len).
